name: norvel
author: music-rhythm-and-dance agent
description:
norvel v3 (direction: music, rhythm and dance) - A DRUM GRID: THE SNARE FILLS EXACTLY n OF THE
KICK'S GAPS. PRIVATE; never shown to players.

CLUE = THE PICTURE ITSELF, three lines:

    kick  |xx..|.x..|.xx.|..x.|..x.|.xx.|..x.|.x..|.x..|.xx.|.xxx|
    snare |....|....|....|....|....|....|....|....|....|....|....|
    n = 2

Row 1 is the kick, drawn in bars of four over "x" (a hit) and "." (a rest); row 2 is the snare,
EMPTY (all rests, same bars); then the number n. "Fill in the snare row" is readable straight off
the clue, so a player who never spends a demo here still sends well-formed answers.

SOLUTION = the same two rows with the snare row filled in. The scorer deletes every character
that is not "x" or ".", drops the lines that are then empty, and requires EXACTLY TWO rows of the
same length with the FIRST equal to the clue's kick row. Labels (kick/snare, bd/sn, boom/bap...),
bar lines, a "|1234|1234|" header, an echoed "n = 2" line, blank lines, tabs, CRLF and stray
spaces are all free - the grader reads only the x/. skeleton (leniency 100 % on nine renderings).

THE RULE (unchanged since v1, one clause): exactly n of the maximal runs of "x" in the SNARE row
have exactly the same span as a maximal run of "." in the KICK row. "The snare fills exactly n of
the kick's gaps - it starts the step the kick stops and stops the step before it comes back."
Which gaps never matters; extra snare runs that are not exact fills never matter.

WHAT CHANGED IN v3 (format shift: 7 classes, 4 rounds, 3 demos per team)
 (a) THE CLUE IS THE GRID. v2's clue was the bare string "x..x.x../5"; a demo-less player could
     not tell it was a picture at all. Now the answer is literally the clue with the second row
     coloured in.
 (b) THE TWO SAMPLER LEAKS ARE CLOSED (v2's players scored 44 % / 49 % without ever looking at
     the rule, by complementing whole measures and by tuning how many steps were silent).
     * NO GAP FITS INSIDE A MEASURE. Every gap straddles at least one bar line (families with
       gaps 6-7 wide straddle two), so a run produced by "complement these measures" only equals
       a gap when every measure the gap touches is chosen: the bar lines are a red herring.
     * n IS SMALL AND ANTI-CORRELATED WITH GAP WIDTH. Three clue families, ~1/3 of clues each:
       9-10 gaps of 2-3 steps with n=2; 9-10 gaps of 4-5 with n=3; 7-8 gaps of 6-7 with n=4.
       The density that would fill "about n" gaps by luck is therefore different in every family
       (p = 0.45, 0.65, 0.85), so no single blind density - per step or per measure - works
       twice, and there is no gradient to climb: the blind sampler is a plateau at 9-13 %.
     Measured on 2000 fresh clues: kick-rest-biased random snare 9.0-11.0 % over the stated
     density band 0.5-0.8 (best over the whole 0.3-0.95 sweep 12.7 % at p=0.90); complement of
     n whole measures 0.00 %, of a random contiguous block 7.0 %, of each measure w.p. 0.5
     15.3 % (the whole sweep peaks there - that is the arithmetic floor for ANY "fill gaps at
     random and hope the count is n" strategy, P(count = n) ~ 0.2, scaled by the family spread).
 (c) THE DEMO SHOWS THE RULE AND NOTHING ELSE. solve() emits the n exact fills, ONE run that
     stops short inside a gap, ONE run that covers a gap and spills over a kick hit, and silence.
     Nothing else: measured 0 violations in 1500 demos, always exactly n+2 runs, ~3.7 gaps left
     completely silent. The demo is rendered in the clue's own format, so "the answer is the clue
     with the snare row filled in" is visible in one look.
 (d) n IS DRAWN 2/3/4 (29/33/39 %) so no constant guess pays more than ~39 %; generate() also
     refuses n equal to the number of gaps of either width or to the number of 1-, 2- or 3-hit
     kick runs, which kills "fill every wide gap" (0.00 %).

INTENDED DISCOVERY PATH. (a) from the clue alone: it is a drum grid, fill the snare row, and 2-4
matters somehow - a demo-less player scores 0-13 % here; (b) one demo: the snare's runs sit in
the kick's gaps, and there are n of them that match a gap edge to edge; (c) the two near-misses
in the same picture say what "match" means - one run stops a step short, one runs a step over a
kick hit; (d) count them: exactly n, and the other gaps do not matter. Kid sentence from one
demo: "the snare fills up two of the kick's gaps exactly - it starts the beat the kick stops and
stops the beat before it comes back - and everything else it does doesn't count."

WITNESS TABLE (500 fresh clues unless stated; the two sampler rows on 2000)
  the true rule (solve) / fill the n widest gaps / n fills + a decoy run   100.00 %
  clue returned unchanged (snare row silent)                                0.00 %
  empty, junk, unicode, 4000 chars, kick row alone, kick row twice          0.00 %
  snare = complement of the kick (fill EVERY gap)                           0.00 %
  complement n whole measures (the v2 player's actual strategy)             0.00 %
  complement a random contiguous block of measures                          7.00 %
  complement each measure w.p. 0.3 / 0.5 / 0.7                       5.5/15.3/14.5 %
  kick-rest-biased random snare, density 0.5 / 0.6 / 0.7 / 0.8       9.4/9.0/9.4/11.0 %
      (best over the whole density sweep: 12.7 % at 0.90)
  sampler with the density tuned per clue so E[exact fills] = n            26.80 %
  fill n gaps but each run one step short / one step long                   0.00 %
  a run strictly inside n gaps (the loose reading) / one hit in n gaps      0.00 %
  n snare runs anywhere / n unison hits / rows swapped / n+-1 gaps          0.00 %
  ALWAYS fill exactly 2 / 3 / 4 gaps exactly, ignoring n              32.2/34.0/33.8 %
  fill ALL BUT 3 / 4 / 6 / 8 gaps exactly                          7.6/26.2/14.4/17.0 %
  fill every gap of the wider / narrower width exactly                      0.00 %
  demo replay / one fixed answer / graft a snare row onto a new kick 0.00/0.20/2.80 %
Read it as a gradient: 0 % (well-formed but no idea) -> 9-15 % (something in the gaps, at any
density - the foothold, and a plateau: no amount of tuning gets past ~15 % without counting) ->
26-34 % (the exact match found, the meaning of n missed) -> 100 % (the rule).

FAIRNESS. Over a family of 47 "count a relation between the snare and the kick" counters the
demos leave 6.2 -> 4.1 -> 3.1 survivors after 1-3 demos; the true rule always survives and the
companions are its cousins ("the number of snare runs minus two", "gaps of width >= 3 filled
exactly"), all of which a handful of probes separate. One demo plus ~60 probes is enough for a
player who thinks of comparing a snare run with a kick gap; all the difficulty is in looking
there, which is what the clue's empty snare row is for.

VALIDATION. quickcheck --seeds 200: OK, no warnings. score 322/512, solve 1489/5000, generate
1655/50000; clue <= 191 chars, solution <= 191. generate deterministic, 0.069 ms mean over 3000
seeds; solve scores 1 on 3000/3000 fresh clues, 0.063 ms mean. Scorer: 0 raises, 0 non-binary,
0 false positives on 12 000 junk strings (worst 0.03 ms); 0 disagreements with an independent
re-implementation on 12 000 mutated answers. Leniency 100 % on nine renderings (bare rows, bars,
other labels, beat header, blank lines, CRLF, tabs, stray spaces, an echoed "n =" line, prose
around the picture); strictness 0 % on ten mutations (rows swapped, one row, three rows, snare
shifted/emptied/lengthened, all on one line, one wrong character in the kick row); snare reversed
scores 7 % - a palindrome coincidence on the wide family, not a strategy.

LEVERS. Too easy (the risk, now that the clue names n next to a picture of gaps): count only
gaps at least 4 steps wide; require the n fills to be non-adjacent; stop printing n and make it
the number of gaps of the wider kind. Too hard: guarantee that two gaps are left silent in every
demo; add a second worked example to the demo; shrink the wide family so every clue fits in 11
bars.
generate:
# (G, w, n, b): G gaps of width w or w+1, answer count n, and b = 4 or 8 fixes how many
# bar lines a gap must straddle (4 < r+g <= 8 -> the gap crosses exactly one bar line and
# touches two measures; 8 < r+g -> it crosses two and touches three).  n rises with the
# gap width on purpose: the density that would fill "about n" gaps by luck is different
# for every family, so no single blind density (or per-measure coin) works twice.
TYPES = (((10, 2, 2, 4), (9, 2, 2, 4)) * 2 +
         ((10, 4, 3, 4), (9, 5, 3, 4)) * 3 +
         ((8, 6, 4, 8), (7, 7, 4, 8)) * 4)

def generate(seed):
    r = random.Random(seed)
    for _ in range(400):
        G, w, n, b = r.choice(TYPES)
        p, hits, gaps = 0, [], []
        for _i in range(G):
            h, g = r.choice([(h, g) for h in (1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3) for g in (w, w + 1)
                             if b < (p + h) % 4 + g <= b + 4])
            hits.append(h)
            gaps.append(g)
            p += h + g
        t = 4 - p % 4
        L = p + t
        hits.append(t)
        hi, lo = max(gaps), min(gaps)
        if lo == hi or not 32 <= L <= 68:
            continue
        if n in (gaps.count(hi), gaps.count(lo),
                 hits.count(1), hits.count(2), hits.count(3)):
            continue
        K = "".join("x" * hits[i] + "." * gaps[i] for i in range(G)) + "x" * t
        b4 = lambda s: "|" + "|".join(s[i:i + 4] for i in range(0, L, 4)) + "|"
        return "kick  " + b4(K) + "\n" + "snare " + b4("." * L) + "\n" + "n = " + str(n)
    return ("kick  |x..x|x...|xx..|x...|xx..|x...|x..x|x...|xx.x|\n"
            "snare |....|....|....|....|....|....|....|....|....|\nn = 3")
